what_was_missing: Nothing was absent. Every section 4 function and constant exists (now 88 exports: the 87 found plus removeFile). Every bracketed section 3 format has its schema file (58 files). All 58 load and pass the closed-keyword check. Every name a script or test imports from lib exists. The shipped tcb/thresholds.json (all section 3.20 names present), profiles/*.json and every fixtures/*/*/case.json validate against their schemas.

Corrected PATTERNS.task to the contract's section 1.5 pattern (device name followed by end or '.'). The draft also refused a device name followed by '-' to fit spec/lib.md T2's 'con-research'. The contract is the source of truth, Win32 reserves only the bare name with or without an extension, and the lib test writer asserted acceptance from the contract.
Corrected realProc().alive: removed the process.kill(pid, 0) ESRCH shortcut. It answered false while PowerShell was unavailable; contract section 4.9 and T89 require null whenever PowerShell fails.

Corrected slotCount (section 4.10, T96). A 'never admitted' filter (no manifest, session or bound_at) ran before the process match. An attempt that had only a folder therefore counted 0 even with a live matching process, and was skipped when procList was null. The order is now the contract's: unconfirmed; procList null -> unknown; a matched process -> live; the current admitted/started/bound attempt or the last attempt of a committed row -> unknown; a transcript -> unknown. Each epoch is counted once. Without a root, a relative attempt folder's transcript is now found through a project folder whose first cwd ends with that folder; before, that check was skipped.

Corrected intakeCandidates' in_flight (spec/check-queue.mjs.md step 2 and T14). A batch whose queue/<b>/ folder exists without batch.json (a cut-off write) is ignored. A batch.json of another mode is ignored ('of the same mode'). A sealed key with no queue folder still counts.

Completed validate's cross-file $ref resolution. With no run root known (a schema not loaded through loadSchema and no opts.root), it now reads the schemas folder beside lib.mjs (= <root>/tcb/schemas). `resolve` may also be a string naming a run root or a schemas folder, as well as a function. A missing file or definition is still an error entry, never a throw.

parseTranscript memory: the run-text buffer kept the text blocks of every message id in an assistant run; it now keeps only the last id's (turnEnds unchanged). This matters for T79b (50 MB under a small heap).

parseTranscript entry shapes: `open: true` on the end-of-file turn end is now non-enumerable, so turnEnds entries are exactly the contract's {ts, text}. Added `line` (the 1-based line of the parse, the file's line when fromByte is 0) to tool uses, tool results and structured entries, also non-enumerable. U2a asked for it for harvest's source.line, and harvest already reads s.line. JSON output and deep equality see only the contract fields.

currentDesign now returns exactly the contract's {cut_sha, hazards_id, hazards_sha}. The stpa/fmea choice by the same highest-commit-seq rule (U1a's request; the draft returned stpa_id and fmea_id as plain keys) rides along as non-enumerable stpa_id, stpa_sha, fmea_id and fmea_sha.
checkerVerdicts now returns exactly {verdicts, reasons, duplicates, unknown_items}. The draft's extra `details` and `unknown_ids` are now non-enumerable (no script reads them).

child_process is now used through its default export (cp.execFileSync, cp.spawnSync), looked up at call time like fs. A test that patches the module's properties (T88's spy, the fs-seam tests per the lib test notes) reaches the library.

paths(root): added the keys builders asked for: commitRecord(task, step), statusDir, cutFile(sha), heldoutOf(field), plantKey(task), plantDir(task), blindKey(sha), frozenFile(name, sha), protocolDraft(field), plantCandidatesOf(field), auditFile(task, e), auditSearch(task, e), auditCoordinator(ce), snapshotRaw/snapshotText(sha) (no extension, as snap.mjs writes them), snapshotMeta(sha), byUrlFile(key). Existing keys are unchanged.
Added export removeFile(path, opts?): unlink with the section 4.3 sharing retries; an absent file returns false (U1a's request for stop.mjs).
Schema repair.schema.json: causes[].card_id may be null. tms.mjs writes null for causes that name no card (pack-repaired, questions-changed), which the draft schema refused (U2b's request).

Schema by-url.schema.json: section 3.13's 'reason is required when raw_sha is null' is now enforced with an anyOf (raw_sha a string, or reason present). The draft's description claimed it could not be expressed in the subset.
deviations_from_the_spec: spec/lib.md T2 lists `--task con-research` as exit 66; the library follows CONTRACT section 1.5 and accepts it (the contract wins; spec/lib.md names the contract as its source of truth).

projectDirName replaces every non-alphanumeric character with '-' (kept from the draft). The contract lists ':', '\\', '/', '.', '_' and space. The result is identical on those characters and on T82's example; other characters (e.g. non-ASCII) are also replaced, as the harness is believed to do.

parseTranscript takes a parseable last line that lacks a trailing newline as a record and moves endByte past it (kept from the draft). The contract says endByte is the end of the last complete line. A truncated JSON object never parses, so a torn line is still torn (T78), and a later parse from that endByte starts at the newline and skips the empty line.
intakeCandidates' in_flight follows spec/check-queue.mjs.md (batch.json present, same mode) on top of CONTRACT 4.10's shorter wording.
slotCount takes an optional 4th argument {root} that is not in the contract's signature; all current callers pass three arguments.

currentProtocol accepts a ledger sha256 that equals either the sha of the frozen file's bytes or the sha of its canonical form, and accepts a root-relative or absolute `path`. The contract leaves both forms open (U2a test note).

Extra fields beyond the contract's shapes are non-enumerable (parse `line`, turn-end `open`, currentDesign's stpa/fmea fields, checkerVerdicts' details). The enumerable extras kept from the draft are parseTranscript's `reset`, readLedger's `badLines`, fence's `changed` and `rev`, and calls' `partial` flag.

A lock file whose record does not parse (a holder that died between its wx create and its write) is never judged stale, because section 4.4 defines staleness only through proc.alive(pid, start_time). Every acquirer then waits and exits 75 until a person removes the file. This is unchanged from the draft and is fail-safe.

slotCount with procList null now counts every attempt that is not known ended (stop not confirmed, row not planned), as the contract says. That includes an attempt entry that `fence --reason first` created and that never ran, for example on a row cut before any start. While PowerShell fails, such entries hold a slot as unknown forever. This is fail-safe (admission refuses), but status shows more unknown slots than are real. A narrower rule needs a contract change.

intakeCandidates: if check-queue is cut off after writing the sealed key and before creating queue/<b>/, the key alone keeps those cards in flight until `--requeue`. The rule cannot tell that case from a lib-test fixture that has a seed key and no queue folder.

T79b (50 MB parsed under a small heap) depends on the fixture's shape. The parser keeps every call, tool use (with its input), result (up to 2,000 characters) and turn-end text, as the contract requires. A fixture whose bulk sits in tool inputs or turn-end text can still exceed a 64 MB heap.

parseTranscript's turnEnds text is the joined text blocks of the last message id of the run, not literally of the last record. The harness writes one record per content block, so the last record of a final message may hold only a tool_use; the message-level join is the intended 'last assistant message'.

The lib test notes say tests patch node:fs and node:child_process properties and call syncBuiltinESMExports. The library reads fs through its default export everywhere (FS = fs at call time unless setFsSeam was used) and now reads child_process the same way, so both seams reach it.
